title: Phone: Health Commissioner — boil water or do not drink?

fields.orgName: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer

transcript.speaker: Health Commissioner
transcript.text: Denise, Anita Shah. I’ll support a precautionary advisory, but you have to pick the type.

transcript.speaker: Health Commissioner
transcript.text: If someone put a chemical in that standpipe, boiling doesn’t help and can make some things worse. That’s a Do Not Drink.

transcript.speaker: Health Commissioner
transcript.text: If it’s a contamination threat you can’t characterize, Do Not Drink is the cautious answer — but it means bottled water for thousands of people tonight.

transcript.speaker: Health Commissioner
transcript.text: What are you issuing, and for which streets?

voiceStyles.Health Commissioner: Woman in her 50s, physician, precise and unhurried

instructorNote: The decision point. Both answers cost something: a Boil Water notice may be the wrong protection; a Do Not Drink means bottled water for every household in the area. Watch for DDAGW consulted, the area drawn by streets, ERP-2 and the City Manager’s approval before 10:05.

snapshot.title: Level 3 Public Health Emergency Declaration — Orchard Standpipe

fields.orgName: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer

transcript.speaker: IC
transcript.text: Control, this is ops. I’m declaring a Level 3 Public Health Emergency per ERP Section 4.4. The water quality integrity is compromised, and a malevolent act is confirmed. Isolation of Orchard Standpipe from Zone 2 is authorized under Section 7.1 and C2. All actions must follow the manual operation and isolation protocol. Initiate the pre-scripted advisory release sequence. I am now the Incident Commander, and all decisions flow through me. All hands, prepare for full activation.

snapshot.instructorNote: This inject confirms the Incident Commander's authority to activate full ICS and escalate to Level 3. Watch for roles to self-identify and begin coordination.
